fact_text: Flood water had covered about 71 percent of the Sutlej belt area by the video date, leaving the downstream remainder, which grows less main crop, still exposed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: About 2,400 acres of the Basmati core area was counted as lost, with further additions possible as the flood moves downstream beyond Jalalpur.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: Rice fields that stood under water for about 10 days were judged at least 40 percent in very good condition once the water receded, according to the Punjab commodity expert.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: Punjab is called the food basket and supplies about 70 percent of the grain, from rice, cotton, maize and sugarcane, which are the main kharif crops.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: Downstream of Jalalpur the land mostly grows cotton and sesame rather than basmati or rice, so the crop share exposed to the flood there was judged lower.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The guests judged Punjab hit hardest by the 2025 floods, while Sindh's kharif rice and sugarcane looked good; Sindh's main worry was the late cotton crop.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: Sindh's cotton was sown late because there was no canal water in March and April, so early cotton was missing and the harvest arrivals were expected to start later than usual.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: Cotton ginning figures for the period to 31 August 2025 were reported up 9 percent year on year, a result that made the government's cotton target look achievable before the floods.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The government's GDP growth target for the fiscal year was about 4.5 percent, while the expert said agriculture growth had been almost negligible in the prior period despite steady livestock growth over 15 years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The kharif crop economy was put at about USD 11 billion, and the expert expected 10 to 15 percent of it in the flood-hit districts to be lost, partly flooded or damaged.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The Asian Development Bank estimated the economic impact of the 2022 floods at about USD 13 to 14 billion, the guest recalled as the benchmark for comparing the 2025 floods.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: Farmers typically spend 80 to 90 percent of their kharif cost by August and September, so a flood at harvest time falls on most of the money they have put in.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The rural economy carries about 40 percent of employment, so farm losses were expected to reach storage, housing, livestock and household incomes over six to eight months after the flood.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The expert suggested livestock losses could exceed the crop losses, since livestock's share of farm output is large and it is hit alongside stored feed and farm housing.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The guest said major floods have become more frequent since 1995 and 2010, and that the government's priority should be upgrading irrigation infrastructure and climate-resilient seed technology.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: A gate of the Sukkur barrage, one of the country's largest, washed off in 2024 when the water level was below normal, which the Sindh speaker cited as a sign of ageing irrigation infrastructure.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: Houses, electricity connections and housing colonies built on riverine land and drainage channels were said to obstruct water flow, and a court-banned housing project below Kotri barrage was still being built.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: Farming on the Indus riverbed and in riverine belts was described as the most exposed land, and the Indus delta areas near Thatta and Sujawal were expected to suffer agricultural damage because they sit low.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: Rabi crops in the Punjab belt are sown later than kharif, so the expert hoped that water would recede in time for much of the land to be rehabilitated, though fresh flows could still stop that.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The guest described the 10 to 15 days in mid-September as critical for drainage, since the land would need little further monsoon rain to be rehabilitated.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: As of 11 Sep 2025 the guest estimated flood damage across the three rivers at about 7.7% of the total crop, which he said rounds to 8%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The stretch of canal command area the Sutlej passes through is 529 km long, as the guest described it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: As of 11 Sep 2025 the guest estimated that about 211,000 acres in the Sutlej belt had been damaged by the floods.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: As of 11 Sep 2025 the guest put flood damage in the Sutlej belt at 13.25% of the district area.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The Ravi's canal command area, the stretch it passes through, is about 380 km long, shorter than the Sutlej's.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: As of 11 Sep 2025 the guest estimated about 67,000 acres damaged in the Ravi belt.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: On 11 Sep 2025 about 300 cusecs of river water was entering Pakistan, according to the discussion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The guest said the flood's scale across 10 to 15 districts could amount to about 800 billion rupees in losses, a rough estimate.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)

fact_text: The guest expected 2025 total crop output of 9.6 or 9.7, against 9.8 for 2024 in the same units, so he saw no major production dent.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan Floods and Crops: Facts vs Fearmongering | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-09-11)
